title: Claude Code loops automate tasks with four levels of control from manual to #AI #Automation #Coding
description: Anthropic’s new guide on using loops in Claude Code outlines four progressively advanced loop types that automate repetitive tasks by cycling through work until predefined stop conditions are met. The first type is a manual, turn-based loop where users prompt Claude and review outputs step-by-step. The second type introduces goal-based loops, which run continuously until a specified objective—such as improving a Lighthouse score—is achieved or a maximum number of attempts is reached, validated by an evaluator model that prevents premature stopping. The third type adds time-based automation, running prompts at regular intervals locally or in the cloud via scheduled loops, enabling continuous checks and updates without manual intervention. The most advanced, fourth type, combines goal, schedule, and workflow elements for fully autonomous operation, allowing Claude to execute multi-step processes, explore parallel solutions, and self-assess outcomes without human input. The guide emphasizes starting simple and scaling loop complexity only as needed, balancing efficiency with practical task requirements. This structured approach enhances productivity by tailoring automation complexity to task demands, enabling developers and teams to incrementally leverage AI-driven workflows while maintaining control and oversight. It supports versatile use cases from basic iterative prompting to complex, hands-free operations, underscoring the value of adaptable AI orchestration in software development and maintenance. #ClaudeCode #AIautomation #Anthropic #LoopAutomation #AITools #SoftwareDevelopment #ProductivityTools #CodeAutomation #ArtificialIntelligence #DeveloperTools #TaskAutomation #WorkflowManagement #GoalBasedLoops #TimeBasedAutomation #CloudScheduling
